subject: Energy
title: Spent Fuel Storage
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Spent Fuel Storage.

hook.text: Spent fuel is first stored in cooling pools at the reactor site—water absorbs both heat and radiation.

buildup.text: After 5–10 years, fuel is cool enough for dry cask storage—sealed in steel and concrete containers on site.

discovery.text: Dry casks are passively cooled—no electricity or pumps needed, just air circulation through the concrete shell.

twist.text: Most spent fuel worldwide sits in 'temporary' storage at reactor sites—some has been there for over 40 years.

climax.text: Dry casks are remarkably robust—designed to withstand earthquakes, floods, tornadoes, and even aircraft impacts.

punchline.text: Temporary for decades—because permanent storage keeps getting delayed.

quiz.question: How are dry spent fuel casks cooled?
